assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is an enabling method that rebuilt how aryl amines are made and is embedded in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis worldwide. The impact is broad, original and clearly demonstrable, which fits the enabling-method criterion I weigh most.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic reactions and mechanistic understanding. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precedent but the practical catalytic amination came from the two. A two-person prize is clean, though the Kosugi precedent needs a citation.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of independent confirmation, industrial scale use and stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue, and it follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize without overlapping it.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs the Kosugi precedent against the 1994-95 catalytic work
Possible reluctance to reward a further cross-coupling topic after 2010

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes opened a large, designable family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides whose composition and surface terminations can be tuned for energy storage, conductivity and EMI shielding. It is a new materials class with architecture-to-function logic, which I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Drexel discovery of Ti3C2 by Naguib, Gogotsi, Barsoum and coworkers is well documented, and Barsoum's MAX-phase foundation is decisive. Three names map naturally onto the supplied credit. Other contributors to later MXene chemistry are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of very wide independent replication, with a stable structural picture of the 2D layers. Application impact is still emerging and surface-termination structure is only partly resolved by direct structural methods, so some maturity risk remains.
uncertainties: Surface termination and defect structure are hard to determine and vary by synthesis
Practical applications remain early compared with the volume of papers

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns a small molecule into a tool that hijacks the ubiquitin-proteasome system, making formerly undruggable proteins addressable. It is a genuinely new chemical concept with clinical candidates now in late stage trials.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first demonstrations come from Crews and Deshaies, with Ciulli providing structure-guided ligand design for VHL and degrader mechanism. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a separate story, so this is a compound discovery whose parts could need different recognition and a three-name cut leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across many labs. Clinical validation is not yet complete, so timing may be premature compared with the more mature candidates.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological nitrogen fixation, and the structure of its FeMo cofactor, including the interstitial carbide, is a structural-chemistry problem of the first rank. I strongly value structural evidence on a complex metal cluster and the mechanism it explains.
assessment.attribution: Rees provided the foundational crystal structures, Einsle the high-resolution structure and carbide discovery, and Seefeldt/Dean/Ribbe the biochemical and mechanistic work. The credit is spread across five people and a three-person cut is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site are still being debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Substrate binding mode and the full catalytic cycle are unresolved
Difficult allocation among five credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites produced an extraordinary rise in solar-cell efficiency within a decade and a new class of semiconducting materials. The scientific and technological impact is very large and the structure-property relationship is a materials-chemistry story.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park the first solid-state device with long stability, and Snaith the thin-film efficiency breakthrough and mechanistic understanding. Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok are also strong claimants, so a three-person cut is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Replication is very broad but device stability, toxicity of lead and commercialisation are unresolved, so it may be early.
uncertainties: Contentious attribution among six credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitised nanocrystalline solar cell introduced a molecular, photochemical approach to photovoltaics and inspired later hybrid and perovskite devices. It is original and influential, with structure-function thinking on mesoporous oxide films.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the clear primary credit. Hagfeldt contributed mostly later development and mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over 30 years with a stable picture. Commercial impact stayed modest, which tempers worthiness, and the field has moved partly to perovskites.
uncertainties: Whether recognition is better combined with perovskites

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ordered mesoporous silica extended templated synthesis from zeolites to the mesopore range, enabling designed pore architectures for catalysis, adsorption and later materials. It also drove advances in structure determination of porous solids. Close to my own field, so I judge it carefully rather than generously.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil team (Kresge, Beck) discovered M41S, Inagaki independently reported FSM-16, and Stucky with Zhao contributed SBA-15 and broader mechanisms. Priority and allocation among Mobil, Japanese and US groups is not simple.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely confirmed, but it is about thirty years old and the practical impact has been more modest than for zeolites, so the case may have weakened.
uncertainties: Priority among Mobil, Inagaki and Stucky groups

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs lets one determine structures from nanocrystals and follow reactions in time, which is a method that enabled a community to see what it could not before. It resonates with my own work on small crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the experimental demonstration and diffraction-before-destruction concept, and Fromme the early photosystem work. Hajdu and Schlichting are also significant, and spelling out a two-name cut leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Well demonstrated and reproduced, but the method relies on very few large facilities and many results have been later matched by synchrotron and microED methods, so the lasting impact is still being established.
uncertainties: Dependence on a small number of facilities
Allocation among Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu, Schlichting and others
